newsitem.title: UK: Ivory coast to destroy some cocoa/coffee trees.
newsitem.headline: Ivory coast to destroy some cocoa/coffee trees.

text.p: Ivorian commodities minister Guy-Alain Gauze said on Monday the government had decided to destroy all coffee and cocoa planted illegally in national forests.
Speaking to reporters at the International Cocoa Organization talks Gauze said that these illegal plantings had amounted to around 100,000 tonnes of cocoa and coffee last year.
"We will destroy all this anarchic production, with immediate effect," he said.
"The decision was taken at a ministerial council last Friday," he added.
"This is a big problem,' he said. "This is explains the gap between our production forecasts and the eventual outcome,' he added.

Gauze, who earlier said the crop would be less than one million tonnes, added that taking account of the destruction of illegally planted trees, the crop would be between 900,000 and 950,000 tonnes for 1996/97.
He also said that the farmers who plant in these illegal areas would receive no compensation for the destroyed crops.

Asked whether the government had any decision on the marketing of the mid-crop, which last year totalled as much as 200,000 tonnes, Gauze said "we don't have a specific policy on the mid-crop. We are waiting to see first what local manufacturers are going to process internally, he said.
Gauze also said that world prices did not reflect the fundamental situation of the market.
"I think prices are too low given that we are going to have a deficit of 160,000 to 202,000 tonnes,' he said.
